_why: CHRON is a temporal intelligence surface, not a footer. §6: every countdown is COMPUTED from target_date at render time. Hardcoding '21 hari' or '164 hari' means the number is wrong the next morning and nobody notices — the poster keeps printing a stale number with full confidence. Both lanes were doing exactly that.
_rule: No renderer may print a day-count that is not (target_date - render_date).days. The build self-test proves this by rendering twice, ten days apart, and failing if the numbers do not move.

_fields.target_date: ISO date in the event's own timezone
_fields.timezone: IANA name; deltas are computed against the render date in this zone
_fields.title: what the reader sees
_fields.audience: who this is relevant to — arif | syed | both
_fields.source: where the date comes from; a date with no source is a rumour
_fields.confidence: HIGH | MEDIUM | LOW, about the DATE itself not the event
_fields.consequence: HIGH | MEDIUM | LOW if the date passes unnoticed
_fields.actionability: HIGH | MEDIUM | LOW — can the reader do anything before it lands
_fields.note: one line of why it matters, written for the shared audience

_expiry_law: An event whose target_date is in the past LEAVES the active pool. It does not render as '0 hari' or a negative count. It moves to history with state MISSED or FULFILLED. A stale countdown on a poster is a lie printed once a day.
